title: Dropping the duplicate start state
subtitle: Every RM with a rule clause starts in a state that only exists before the first step. It behaves exactly like the state an idle step leads to, so we drop it.

items: **Which RMs:** 19 of the 25 reward-step test RMs, every task with at least one rule clause (Absence, Precedence, Response, ChainResponse, RespondedExistence, NotCoExistence). Goal-only tasks are unchanged.

**The rule:** if the start is never re-entered and, on every input, goes to the same state with the same reward as its idle successor, the idle successor becomes the start and the old start is removed. Otherwise nothing changes.
**What stays the same:** every reward, every episode total, the well, the final. Only the state count and the state numbers change.
**What goes away:** the "idle first step pays 0" special case, and one near-duplicate state description and embedding per RM.

items: **Expected RMs** are built from today's compiler output by removing the start when the rule above allows it (`check/start_merge_check.py expect`).

**The check** walks the expected RM and the new compiler RM side by side on every input from the start, pairing states one to one: same rewards, same final and well, same state count. One extra state, a changed reward, or a lost final fails it (tested on purpose).
**Also rerun:** the 253 reward-step checks (episode totals) and the unit tests.
